subject: Inject a request-scoped opportunistic-drain loop directive in classify-assemble.js (substantive prompts)
description:
Make the loop the DEFAULT for substantive prompts so judgment (and other housekeeping) rides the loops user requests already spawn — no always-on session, cost bounded to real work. ADD ONLY; do not replace existing parts.

DESIGN (user, 2026-06-14): every UserPromptSubmit already relays to /classify → assembleClassifyResponse (lib/classify-assemble.js), which builds the injected additionalContext from a parts[] list. Today it has HEARTBEAT (slow 2h ScheduleWakeup keepalive) + buildJudgeNudge (single-shot "dispatch ONE judge subagent this turn", declinable). The agent declines it. The fix: inject a DIRECTIVE that the agent works the request AS A LOOP, and the existing per-tick judge pressure drains inside the loop.

WHY it's a small ADD: once an agent is in the loop (orch-loop skill / loop_control), each tick calls next_action → daemon decideOne, which ALREADY emits action:'judge_eager' (eager marks) + 'judge_edges' (standing queue). So the loop already drains the judge queue — no new drain logic. The only missing thing is telling the agent to START the loop by default.

DO:
1. In lib/classify-assemble.js assembleClassifyResponse, ADD a new parts.push([Loop] directive) — do NOT remove HEARTBEAT or buildJudgeNudge. Gate it on SUBSTANTIVE prompts (use heuristic.decision / complexity — conversational turns skip it; their loop would self-terminate anyway, but avoid the noise).
2. Directive text (tune wording): "[Loop] Work this request as a loop (orch-loop skill). Each iteration: advance the request; on slack (waiting on subagents / between steps), drain eager-judge marks FIRST, then up to K standing-queue items. The loop's next_action surfaces this work (judge_eager / judge_edges). Continue until the request is satisfied, then stop. Do NOT run forever — end when the request is done."
3. The opportunistic standing-queue part MUST be SLACK-CAPPED (K per iteration, config) so housekeeping never out-spends the user's request — this is the "doesn't eat user's cost" guarantee. Eager marks (the user's own freshly-wired nodes) are priority; standing queue is best-effort/capped.
4. Keep it additive + behind the existing orchGateOff check (no loop directive when orch is off).

TEST: a substantive prompt's /classify additional_context now contains the [Loop] directive + still contains HEARTBEAT + the judge nudge; a conversational prompt does NOT get the loop directive; orchGateOff suppresses it. Run the classify/assemble tests.

BLOCKED BY the eager-mark lease task (concurrent loops would double-judge without it) — see sibling task. Files: lib/classify-assemble.js (+ maybe prompt-heuristic for the substantive gate). No daemon restart needed for the inject text (the /classify endpoint reads it live) but confirm.
